answer: Comet-Horizon Admission Windows. Each identity must submit its first N messages within a fixed arrival window; the system scores inter-arrival spacing against a required burst-then-pause shape. Sybils created in bulk emit near-identical timing, so their traffic fails the shape test and is throttled to a velvet trickle of one message per long horizon. To pass, an attacker must rent distinct machines and pace each identity's traffic by hand over days, paying real compute and labor per identity rather than a one-time fee.
